title: Camels store water in their humps?

segments.text: Camels store water in their humps. Well, that's not exactly true. The hump is full of fat.
A hump can hold up to {80|eighty} pounds of fat, which the camel burns for energy when food runs out.
When a camel goes hungry for a long time, the hump actually shrinks and flops over to one side.
Here's the wild part. A thirsty camel can drink about {30|thirty} gallons of water in just {13|thirteen} minutes.
That's not all. Its red blood cells are oval, so they keep flowing when the camel is dried out, and they can swell up without bursting.
In fact, a camel can lose a quarter of its body weight in water and still survive. That would kill most other animals.
So the hump isn't a water bottle. It's a lunchbox.
